name: Bhimtal and Sattal
tagline: Kumaon's quieter lakes, oak forest and the best birding near Kathgodam
meta_description: Bhimtal, Sattal and Naukuchiatal: lake walks, dawn birding, kayaking, real costs and where to stay, 22 km from Kathgodam station in Kumaon.
summary: Bhimtal is the largest lake in Kumaon, 22 km from Kathgodam at about 1,370 m, and Sattal's chain of small forest lakes lies 10 km west of it. Come for calm lakeside stays, kayaking, and some of the best morning birding in the lower Himalaya. Two to three nights works well for families and birders.
intro: Bhimtal is what Nainital was before the crowds. The lake covers about 47.8 hectares, the largest by surface area in Kumaon, and sits lower and warmer at about 1,370 m. An island near the southern dam holds a small aquarium reached by boat, and the stone Bhimeshwar Mahadev shrine stands near the dam. The town has grown around the lake road, but it remains a working tehsil town, not a resort strip.

Ten kilometres west, Sattal is a cluster of seven small lakes in a fold of oak and pine forest at about the same height. The names are local: Panna or Garud Tal, Naldamyanti Tal, Ram, Sita and Laxman Tal, Hanuman Tal and the dry Sukha Tal. In the British period part of the area was a tea estate, one of four in Kumaon. Today it is known among birders for barbets, woodpeckers, blue magpies and forktails along its streams.

Naukuchiatal, the nine-cornered lake, is 4 km east of Bhimtal and the third piece of this lake country. Together they make a good base for families who want water and short walks without Nainital's traffic, and for birders who want dawn on the forest edge. Kathgodam station is under an hour away, so this is also the easiest first or last night of a Kumaon trip.
facts: ≈ 22 km · 45 min to Bhimtal; ≈ 32 km · 1 h to Sattal

highlights.title: Boat to Bhimtal's island
highlights.text: Rowing and pedal boats cross to the small island near the southern end of the lake, which holds a public aquarium. The ride takes about 10 minutes each way. Mornings are calmer; afternoon wind on the open lake can make pedal boats hard work.

highlights.title: Dawn birding at Sattal
highlights.text: Walk the forest road between the lakes from first light. Red-billed blue magpie, great and blue-throated barbets, several woodpeckers and kingfishers are common. A local birding guide knows the stream edges where forktails and thrushes feed.

highlights.title: Kayak on Naukuchiatal
highlights.text: Naukuchiatal, 4 km from Bhimtal, is deep, quiet and less boated than the bigger lakes. Kayaks and boats are hired at the shore. Operators here also run tandem paragliding from the ridge in dry months; check safety and licences first.

highlights.title: Sattal Christian Ashram
highlights.text: Founded in 1930 by the American missionary E. Stanley Jones on a former tea estate by the lakes, the ashram still runs retreats. Its stone chapel and orchards are a short walk from the main lake; visit respectfully and ask before entering buildings.

highlights.title: The Bhimeshwar shrine
highlights.text: On the southern shore by the dam, the old stone Bhimeshwar Mahadev shrine is tied to the local tradition that Bhima of the Mahabharata struck the ground with his mace to bring water. It is a quiet stop on an evening lake walk.

field_notes.fact: Bhimtal's 13th-century history is political as well as sacred: the Chand ruler Trilok Chand built a fort at Bhimtal at a time when Nainital itself still lay outside Chand control.
The Sattal Christian Ashram was set up in 1930 by the American evangelist E. Stanley Jones on a former tea estate beside the lakes, and still runs as a retreat with its own chapel.
Bhimtal lake covers about 47.8 hectares, the largest lake by surface area in Kumaon, and its island lies about 91 metres from the southern dam.

local_word.meaning: wild bayberry, sold in leaf cones by the Bhimtal and Bhowali roads in May and June

Kayak, 30 minutes on Sattal or Naukuchiatal

how_to_reach.text: Pantnagar Airport is about 55 km away, 1.5 hours by taxi through Haldwani. A taxi costs roughly ₹2,000–3,000.

Kathgodam railway station is 22 km from Bhimtal. Shared taxis run from the station and from Haldwani for about ₹100–150 a seat; a private taxi costs ₹800–1,200. For Sattal, hire a taxi from Bhimtal or Bhowali, as there is no regular shared service.

From Delhi, drive about 300 km via Moradabad and Haldwani, then take the Bhimtal road from Kathgodam rather than the Nainital road. Uttarakhand Roadways buses from Delhi go to Haldwani and some continue to Bhimtal. Check current status before you travel in the monsoon.

where_to_stay: Saver: guesthouses and homestays along the Bhimtal lake road start around ₹2,000 a night for a double, and the KMVN tourist rest house at Sattal is a simple option by the lakes. Several camps at Sattal offer tents with shared facilities. Comfort: Bhimtal and Naukuchiatal have mid-range resorts with lake views; pick one away from the main road for quiet. There is no luxury tier here, so signature trips usually stay in Nainital or Mukteshwar and visit Sattal for a morning of birding.
tips: For birding, be on the Sattal road by 6 am and walk slowly; most activity ends by 10 am.
Do not feed the monkeys at Sattal, and keep food inside the car.
Rent kayaks only where life jackets are provided and worn.
Bhimtal is a good first night if your train reaches Kathgodam late in the evening.
Carry your rubbish out from Sattal; the lakes are small and the bins overflow on weekends.

experiences.title: Dawn birding walk around Sattal
experiences.cost: Guide ₹1,500–3,000 per group; taxi from Bhimtal ₹600–900 return
experiences.summary: Sattal's mix of oak forest, pine, streams and small lakes draws a long list of Himalayan birds within an easy walk. A slow dawn walk with a local guide is the best introduction to Kumaon's birdlife, whether you are a beginner with binoculars or a photographer with a long lens.
body: Sattal lies at about 1,370 m, low enough to hold birds of the warmer foothill forest and high enough for mountain species, especially in winter when birds move downhill. Common sightings include red-billed blue magpie, great barbet, blue-throated barbet, slaty-headed parakeet, several woodpeckers including the greater yellownape, and kingfishers on the lake edges.

Most birders start at the forest road below the lakes and walk towards the Christian Ashram, then follow the stream that drains the lakes. Local guides from Sattal and nearby villages know where birds feed at different seasons, and many keep simple feeding and water points used by photographers. Ask how they work before you agree a price, and whether they use playback; we prefer guides who do not.

Winter, from November to March, brings altitudinal migrants such as thrushes and forktails to the streams. April and May are the breeding season and birds are vocal. The monsoon is wet and leeches appear, though the forest is green. Wear dull colours, bring binoculars, carry water and keep voices low. A field guide or a phone app helps with identification.

faqs.q: What birds can I see at Sattal?
faqs.a: Regular species include red-billed blue magpie, great and blue-throated barbets, slaty-headed parakeet, several woodpeckers, laughingthrushes, tits and kingfishers. Winter adds thrushes and forktails that move down from higher forest. A local guide raises your count considerably.

faqs.q: When is the best season for birding at Sattal?
faqs.a: November to May is best. Winter brings altitudinal migrants and clear mornings; April and May bring breeding calls and plumage. July and August are wet, with leeches and fewer visiting birders.

faqs.q: Do I need a guide for birding at Sattal?
faqs.a: You can walk the road alone, but a local guide knows feeding spots, stream edges and calls, and will usually double what you see. Expect ₹1,500–3,000 per group for a half day; agree the route and whether playback is used before starting.

experiences.title: Bhimtal lake walk, island and old shrine
experiences.cost: Boat ₹250–500 per boat; aquarium entry small fee
experiences.summary: Walk the shore of Kumaon's largest lake, take a boat to the island aquarium, and end at the Bhimeshwar Mahadev shrine by the dam as evening lamps are lit. It is an easy, unhurried outing that suits families and older travellers.
body: Start at the northern end where the town meets the lake and walk south along the lake road. The water covers about 47.8 hectares, so a full loop is long; most people walk the eastern shore to the dam, about 1.5 km. The lake is said to take its name from Bhima of the Mahabharata, and the Skanda Purana's Manaskhanda describes this lake district as Chhakhata, the land of sixty lakes.

Boats leave from the jetty near the dam for the island, which lies about 91 metres off the southern embankment and has a small public aquarium. The boat ride is short and calm in the evening. Fees for the aquarium and boats change, so read the posted rates. Life jackets are provided.

Finish at the stone Bhimeshwar Mahadev shrine on the southern shore. Local tradition holds that the Pandavas consecrated it after Bhima opened the spring that filled the lake. Remove shoes before entering, and avoid photographs of worshippers. Snack stalls near the dam sell roasted corn and tea, and in May and June you will see kafal berries sold in leaf cones.

faqs.q: Is Bhimtal better than Nainital for families?
faqs.a: For a calm stay, often yes. Bhimtal is about 22 km from Kathgodam, warmer, less crowded and easier to drive. Nainital has more sights and shopping, so many families stay at Bhimtal and visit Nainital for a day.

faqs.q: How do I get to the island in Bhimtal lake?
faqs.a: Take a rowing or pedal boat from the jetty near the dam. The ride is about 10 minutes. The island holds a small aquarium with a modest entry fee. Boats and fees follow posted rates.

faqs.q: What is the story behind the Bhimeshwar shrine?
faqs.a: Local tradition says that during their exile the Pandavas passed through these hills, Bhima struck the ground with his mace to release water for Draupadi, and they consecrated the Bhimeshwar Mahadev shrine on the shore. The lake is named after Bhima.

experiences.title: A morning kayak on Naukuchiatal
experiences.cost: Kayak ₹300–500 for 30 minutes; taxi from Bhimtal ₹300–500
experiences.summary: Naukuchiatal, the lake of nine corners, is 4 km beyond Bhimtal and quieter than any lake near Nainital. A morning kayak along its wooded edges, followed by tea on the shore, is a gentle adventure for teenagers and adults alike.
body: The lake's name comes from its nine corners, and local belief says that seeing all nine at once brings good luck, though the shape makes that hard from any one point. It lies slightly lower than Bhimtal and is surrounded by oak and pine slopes with a few resorts and homes. In the morning the water is calm and the light is soft.

Single and double kayaks are hired from operators on the shore. Check that life jackets fit and are buckled, and stay within the area the operator shows you. Beginners pick it up in a few minutes; the lake has no current. Rowing and pedal boats are also available for those who prefer to sit.

In the dry months, some operators also sell tandem paragliding from the ridge above the lake. If you try it, ask about the pilot's licence and insurance, and fly only in calm morning conditions. Afterwards, walk part of the shoreline path and watch for kingfishers and cormorants, which are common here.

faqs.q: Is kayaking at Naukuchiatal safe for beginners?
faqs.a: Yes, in calm conditions with a properly fitted life jacket. The lake has no current and operators show you where to paddle. Avoid windy afternoons and stay near the shore if you are not a confident swimmer.
The name means the lake of nine corners, after its irregular shape. Local belief holds that seeing all nine corners at once brings good fortune.

Private operators sell tandem flights in dry months, mainly March to June and October to November. Ask to see licences and insurance, fly in the morning, and skip it if the wind picks up. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Bhimtal or Nainital better to stay in?
faqs.a: Bhimtal is calmer, cheaper and closer to Kathgodam, with easier driving; Nainital has more sights, shops and old buildings. Families and birders often prefer Bhimtal or Sattal and visit Nainital, 22 km away, for a day. In May and June the difference in crowds is large.

faqs.q: How far is Sattal from Bhimtal and Nainital?
faqs.a: Sattal is about 10 km from Bhimtal and about 22 km from Nainital via Bhowali, roughly 30–50 minutes by road. There is no regular shared taxi, so hire a car from Bhimtal or Bhowali.

faqs.q: What can I do in Sattal?
faqs.a: Birding walks at dawn, boating and kayaking on the main lake, visiting the Christian Ashram founded in 1930, walking to the Subhash Dhara spring, and sitting by the water. It is a place for slow mornings rather than sightseeing.

Yes, it is one of the best-known birding spots in the Kumaon foothills. Barbets, woodpeckers, blue magpies, kingfishers and laughingthrushes are regular, and winter brings thrushes and forktails. Go between November and May at first light.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Bhimtal and Sattal?
faqs.a: October to June. Winter mornings are cold but clear and best for birds; March to May is warm and green. July and August bring heavy rain, leeches on forest paths and occasional road damage.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Bhimtal, Sattal and Naukuchiatal?
faqs.a: Two nights is enough for the three lakes at an easy pace, with one dawn birding walk at Sattal. Birders should allow three nights to cover Sattal at different times and perhaps add a day trip to Pangot near Nainital.

faqs.q: Are there budget stays at Bhimtal and Sattal?
faqs.a: Yes. Guesthouses and homestays on the Bhimtal lake road start around ₹2,000 a night for a double, and the KMVN rest house at Sattal is a simple government option. Camps at Sattal offer tents with shared bathrooms.

Yes. It is less than an hour from Kathgodam, the lake road is flat, boats and kayaks suit older children, and the island aquarium is a short ride. Keep children away from the lake edge where there is no railing.

faqs.q: Is there mobile network at Sattal?
faqs.a: Jio and Airtel generally work at Bhimtal and Naukuchiatal. At Sattal the signal is weaker in the forest and near the lower lakes, so download maps and tickets before you go.
